subject: Onramp sprintkick: POC keys & peering
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onramp sprintkick: POC keys & peering

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. As discussed, we want to put a short sprint around a production-like POC so you can validate latency/cost and end-to-end security controls. Attached is an updated mutual action plan (MAP-v2.xlsx) that shows a proposed two-week cadence and responsibilities. High level asks from our side to get the environment wired: 

- Org + project owner (name + email) so we can create an evaluation org and invite your admin.
- API key request: we will issue a scoped test API key for early integration; if you prefer service-account flow we can also issue a temporary SA key.
- IP allowlist ranges (CIDR) OR confirmation you want VPC peering (if peering, we need a contact for cloud networking and preferred maintenance windows).
- Any policy constraints (e.g., IP ranges must be static, egress controls, audit log retention) so we can reflect them in the MAP.

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0–2: org invite + keys + allowlist/peering handshake
- Day 3–7: smoke tests (latency/throughput), function calls, and basic eval prompts
- Day 8–14: workload soak and QA, then go/no-go signoff

Can you confirm the preferred path (allowlist vs peering) and provide the network contact? If you want, we can schedule a 30-min networking sync Tuesday or Wednesday.

Best —
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
202-555-0112

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@novamed.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Onramp sprintkick: POC keys & peering

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks — that timeline looks reasonable. Quick questions before we lock dates: 

1) For our initial test we prefer an IP allowlist to keep things simple. We may want VPC peering for the production rollout, but allowlist is fine for the two-week evaluation.

2) Our networking lead is Sanjay Patel (cc'd). I'll ask him for the small set of egress CIDRs we need to allow. Do you need both IPv4 and IPv6?

3) For the org owner, would you be ok if we provision an evaluation org under our corporate GCP account and then add Redwood as a service principal? Otherwise, we can have Redwood create the sandbox org you mentioned.

We can do a 30-min sync Wednesday 10–10:30am ET if that works for you and Sanjay.

Liam
CTO, NovaMed
liam@novamed.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Onramp sprintkick: POC keys & peering

Ben / Marissa —

Looping you in. NovaMed is leaning to an IP allowlist for the POC (preferred). Action items: 

- Ben: please provision a temporary evaluation org and generate a scoped API key for the "poc-readwrite" role. Put the key in a short text file (temp-api-key.txt) and we'll share via the secure link once we confirm recipients. Also prepare a small curl snippet for the devs.
- Marissa: coordinate a 30-min network call Wednesday 10–10:30am ET with Liam and Sanjay. Share the network_diagram.png during the call and capture the CIDRs they provide.
- Me: I'll update MAP-v2.xlsx to mark owners and shift the kickoff to Wed as tentative.

Please reply with ETA on the key and the meeting invite.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Hi Liam / Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick reply. We're set up to follow the IP-allowlist path for the POC. Deliverables I pushed this morning: 

- Created evaluation org: redwood-eval-novamed (will invite the org owner once you confirm the GCP email).
- Generated scoped API key for the "poc-readwrite" role (temp-api-key.txt). DO NOT paste the key in email — I'll share through the secure artifact link in the meeting.
- Curl example:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"open-llm-3b","input":"hello"}'

Network details we need from your side (Sanjay):
- Exact egress CIDRs (IPv4 preferred). If you have an existing service account to test from, share the source IPs.
- Any required HTTP proxy or outbound NAT that might rewrite source IPs.

I've attached a quick network diagram for the sync (network_diagram.png). I'll join the Wednesday slot and share the secure key after we confirm attendees.

Ben Carter
Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
